title: Making a Complaint
tagline: Which office to use, how to complain clearly, and where to escalate.
description: When a service fails, a clear complaint to the right office gets results. Learn who handles what, how to write a strong complaint, where to escalate, and practise with a real scenario.
outcomes: Match a concern to the office that handles it
Know where to escalate if nothing happens

lessons.title: Which office handles your concern
lessons.body:
A complaint only works if it reaches the office that can act on it.

## Match the concern
Broken water point or drainage, uncollected rubbish, market issues — the local council. Poor treatment at a clinic — the health facility, then the district health office. A document problem — the office that issued it. Unsure — your ward councillor can direct you.

## Get the details
Find the office name and, if you can, a contact person. A complaint sent to the right place is already half-way to being solved.
key_points: Match the concern to the office that can act
Council handles water, rubbish, drainage, markets
Health matters go to the facility, then the district office
Your ward councillor can direct you
lessons.try_it: Write down one concern and the office that should handle it.

lessons.title: Writing a clear complaint
lessons.body:
A strong complaint is short, factual and specific.

## What to include
State what happened, where, and when. Give facts: dates, a location, how many people are affected. Say clearly what you would like done. Keep it polite — it is more persuasive.

## Keep a record
Write or type it and keep a copy. If you hand it in, ask for a stamp or note that it was received. If you send it, keep the message and the date.
key_points: Say what happened, where and when
Give facts: dates, place, people affected
Say clearly what you want done
Keep a copy and proof it was received
lessons.try_it: Draft a three-sentence complaint about a real issue near you.

lessons.title: If nothing happens
lessons.body:
If a complaint is ignored, there are calm next steps.

## Escalate in order
Follow up first and give your reference. If there is still no response, ask for the supervisor or the next office up. Raising it at a community or ward meeting adds weight.

## Keep going, stay calm
Keep your copies and your notes of who you spoke to. A civil society organisation or legal aid service can guide you if you are stuck.
key_points: Follow up and give your reference
Ask for a supervisor or the next office up
Raise it at a community meeting for weight
Keep records; seek help if stuck
lessons.try_it: Write the order of people you would contact if your complaint is ignored.

lessons.title: Scenario: An unresolved problem
lessons.body: Work through a real situation: a service in your area has failed and nothing is happening. Choose what you would do at each step.
key_points: There is often more than one reasonable choice
The feedback explains why one works best

scenario.prompt: The water point serving your street has been broken for three weeks. What is a good first step?
options: Post an angry message in a group chat
Report it to the local council or your ward councillor
Wait and hope someone else reports it
feedback: Venting is understandable, but it does not reach the office that can fix it.
Right — the council or councillor can log the fault and act on it.
If everyone waits, the fault stays unreported and unfixed.

scenario.prompt: The office asks for details. What helps your report most?
options: Just say the water is off
Give the exact location, how long it has been broken, and how many households rely on it
Demand it is fixed today or else
feedback: Too vague — they may not find the right fault.
Yes — specific facts help them act quickly and fairly.
Threats make staff defensive and rarely speed things up.

scenario.prompt: Two weeks later nothing has changed. What now?
options: Follow up with your reference, then ask for a supervisor and raise it at the next ward meeting
Start a fight with the office
feedback: Giving up leaves the problem for everyone.
Right — escalate calmly and add weight by raising it publicly.
Conflict damages the relationship you need to solve this.

quiz.question: A complaint works best when it is sent to:
options: The office that can act on it
quiz.explanation: A complaint only gets results when it reaches the office that can actually act on it.

quiz.question: If your complaint is ignored, a good next step is to:
options: Follow up, then ask for a supervisor or the next office
quiz.explanation: Follow up with your reference, then escalate calmly to a supervisor or the next office up.
